subject: retail-barring-orders-bill-2025
note: The subject is a BILL, so nothing here is a modification to law: the sweep asks what has happened to the TEXT since the print we encoded, and for a Bill that is its passage through Parliament. Two entries, both class 'prospective' and both carrying a currency risk, because the Bill is still before the Legislative Council and the amendments it has already taken in the Assembly are not in the print we hold. Read the coverage_note on each search before treating any of this as a completed sweep: the eleven Supplementary Notice Papers, both Explanatory Memoranda and both second reading speeches were NOT read, and nothing was searched for commentary, litigation or the Bill's treatment outside Parliament.

searches.question: What has happened to Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (Bill No. 47) since the print we hold, and is it law yet?
searches.scope: The Parliament of Western Australia's own bill-progress page for Bill 47 (bills.nsf BillProgressPopup, ParentUNID E606BBEDF543065648258D54000C0BF3), read in full on 2026-09-23: the Status line, both Houses' progress tables with their dates, the document links, and the Supplementary Notice Paper list.
searches.coverage_note: Covers only what the Parliament publishes on that one page. It is NOT a search of: the eleven Supplementary Notice Papers SNP 47-1 to 47-11, which carry the amendments actually proposed in the Council and were not downloaded; either Explanatory Memorandum; either second reading speech; Message No. 50 from the Assembly; Hansard for the Consideration in Detail debate of 2026-03-12, which is where the Assembly's amendments were moved and would be described. It is also not a search for litigation, for commentary, or for any equivalent scheme in another Australian jurisdiction. The page reflects the Parliament's own record-keeping and may lag the Chamber.

searches.question: Which print of the Bill is the file we hold, and does an independent copy exist to check it against?
searches.scope: Internet Archive availability API and CDX index for captures under the Bill's bills.nsf file path, queried 2026-09-23; the 20251231144400 capture of Bill+47-1.pdf was retrieved and its sha256 compared against the local file.
searches.coverage_note: This search found no modification to the text and is recorded as 'no-findings' for that reason, but it is NOT empty of result: it established by digest that the local file is byte-identical to the as-introduced print, which is what entry EM-1 turns on. The Archive holds no capture of Bill+47-1.002.pdf, so the question whether that link serves different bytes could not be answered from the Archive either; direct retrieval from parliament.wa.gov.au is refused by an Azure WAF JavaScript challenge.

entries.summary: The Legislative Assembly considered the Bill in detail and passed it on 2026-03-12 (Consideration in Detail, then Third Reading, both that day; transmitted to the Council by Message No. 50 of the same date). The Parliament's page offers a separate download labelled 'the Bill as passed by originating House'. The encoded text is the as-introduced print of 2025-12-03, so any amendment the Assembly made on 2026-03-12 is absent from it. Whether the Assembly in fact amended the text is not established here — a Bill can be considered in detail and emerge unamended — but the existence of a distinct as-passed print is the Parliament's own signal that the two prints are not assumed identical.

provenance.source: Parliament of Western Australia, Progress of Bills — Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (Bill No. 47)
provenance.citation: Legislative Assembly, Consideration in Detail and Third Reading, 12 March 2026; Message No. 50 from the Legislative Assembly, 12 March 2026

routing.effective_from_absent_reason: Nothing takes legal effect on the Assembly's passage. Under clause 2 the Act would commence as to Part 1 on Royal Assent and as to the rest on a day fixed by proclamation, and neither assent nor any proclamation date exists.

entries.disposition_note: Deferred rather than encoded because the as-passed text was not obtained: direct retrieval of Bill+47-1.002.pdf from parliament.wa.gov.au is refused by an Azure WAF JavaScript challenge, and the Internet Archive holds no capture of it. The correct next step is to obtain that print and diff it against sources/bill-47-1.txt; until that is done, every finding in INCIDENTS.md is a finding about the as-introduced print only, and B-01 and B-02 in particular may already have been repaired in the Assembly. Recorded so that the limitation travels with the work instead of being rediscovered.

entries.summary: The Bill is before the Legislative Council, which agreed the second reading on 2026-09-15, eight days before this sweep. Eleven Supplementary Notice Papers have issued (SNP 47-1 to 47-11, the last current), which are the vehicle for amendments proposed in the Council. The Committee stage had not been reported as complete as at the date of this sweep, so further amendment remains open and the text is not final.

provenance.source: Parliament of Western Australia, Progress of Bills — Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (Bill No. 47)
provenance.citation: Legislative Council, Second Reading Agreed, 15 September 2026; Supplementary Notice Paper SNP 47-11

routing.effective_from_absent_reason: The Bill has not passed the Council, has not received Royal Assent, and its operative Parts commence on proclamation, for which no date exists.

entries.disposition_note: Deferred: the eleven notice papers were not read, so this register cannot say what is proposed, only that amendment is live. SNP 47-11 is the current one and is where anyone relying on this encoding for more than reading the as-introduced text should start. The issue dates of the individual notice papers are not shown on the progress page and were not established.
